newsitem.title: CHINA: China-Taiwan trade up 6.1 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China-Taiwan trade up 6.1 percent in 1996.

text.p: Trade between China and Taiwan totalled $18.98 billion in 1996, up 6.1 percent from 1995, the overseas edition of the People's Daily said on Tuesday.
Taiwanese businessmen pledged to invest $4.38 billion in China in the first nine months of 1996, an increase of 56.6 percent compared with the same 1995 period, the newspaper said.
Actual Taiwanese investment in China in the first three quarters of the year jumped a year-on-year 10 percent to $2.474 billion, the newspaper said.
Chinese authorities approved 2,400 Taiwanese investment ventures during the period, it said without giving further details.
Trade between the two sides, rivals since a civil war split them in 1949, is routed mainly through Hong Kong.
Taiwan has banned direct trade with and investment in China since that year.
